transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for fitting me in. I, um, I hope I'm not wasting your time—it probably sounds a little silly to even bring up. 

But, well, we recently put this new, brighter mirror in our bathroom, and ever since then... I just keep noticing that the skin around my cheeks and my jawline looks really uneven. Or maybe kind of saggy? I guess I've been focusing on it a lot, even though my husband says he can’t really see what I’m talking about at all. 

I know it's probably not a huge deal, and I'm sure other people have much bigger problems, but it's just been bothering me, and I thought I should maybe talk to someone. Does that make sense? I hope that's an okay reason to come in.

Can you tell me a bit more about how much this concern with your cheeks and jawline has been on your mind lately? Has it been distracting you from work, relationships, or other things you usually enjoy?

Oh, well, I want to be clear that I’m definitely still getting all my work done! The attorneys I work for haven't complained or anything, I promise. But, um... I guess it has been on my mind a fair amount. 

I've been spending a little extra time getting ready in the mornings—just trying to smooth things out and do my makeup a bit differently, you know? And because of that, I admit I have had to rush into the courthouse a few mornings lately, which really isn't like me. And... well, I might have missed the very beginning of my yoga class more than once. I feel so silly even saying that out loud. I hope that doesn't sound incredibly vain?

I'm still doing the things I enjoy, mostly. But I suppose I have been avoiding the camera a little bit. Like at my book club or at these community events I help with, I’ll just kind of step out of the frame or offer to take the picture instead. I just don't want to spend the rest of the day worrying about how my face is going to look when they post the photos. I know it sounds shallow, I'm sorry. Is it normal to worry about things like that at my age?

Can you tell me if this concern about your facial appearance ever causes you a lot of distress, even when you're not looking in the mirror or thinking about photos? And if so, how often does that happen?

Oh, um... distress is a strong word, isn't it? I wouldn't say it causes me a lot of distress. I mean, I'm certainly not sitting around crying about it or anything like that. I want to make sure you know I'm handling things okay overall. 

But I suppose... well, maybe sometimes I do think about it when I'm not in front of the mirror. Just a little bit. Like if I'm talking to one of the attorneys at work, or if I'm at the grocery store, I might wonder if the lighting is hitting my face a certain way, or if they're noticing the unevenness. It just kind of pops into my head, you know? 

I wouldn't say it happens constantly. Just... maybe a few times a day? Or maybe a little more on days when I'm feeling particularly tired. I try really hard to just push the thought away and focus on what I'm doing. It's not taking over my life or anything, I promise. I hope that's the kind of information you were looking for? I just don't want to make it sound worse than it really is.
Have you found yourself doing anything repeatedly—like checking mirrors, adjusting your appearance, or seeking reassurance—to try to cope with these thoughts about your face?

Oh, well... I wouldn't say I do anything obsessively. I really don't want you to think I'm just standing around staring at myself all day! I know I have a job to do. 

But, um... most mornings, I suppose I do end up checking my face from a few different angles in that new mirror. Just to make sure everything looks okay. And I might put on just a little extra makeup before I leave for the courthouse, to try and smooth out the unevenness. I just want to look professional for the firm, you know? 

And... well, like I mentioned before, I do try to avoid being in casual pictures if I’m not feeling okay about how my jawline looks that day. And sometimes... I feel a little embarrassed even admitting this, but sometimes I catch myself comparing my face to the other women I see at work. Just looking to see if their skin is doing the same thing mine is. 

But I think most women my age probably do that a little bit, don't they? I really hope I'm not making it sound like I'm completely fixated on it, because I promise I'm not. I hope that answers your question alright?
Can you tell me if there have been times when you felt really upset, anxious, or frustrated specifically about how your face looks, and how long do those feelings usually last?

Oh, upset? Um... I really wouldn't use words like that. I don't get really upset or anxious about it, I promise. I mean, I'm a grown woman, and I know there are much bigger problems in the world than a few wrinkles or some sagging skin, right? 

I guess... well, maybe there are fleeting moments where I feel a tiny bit frustrated if my makeup just isn't sitting right, or if the lighting in the office bathroom is particularly harsh. But it's just a passing thought, really. It doesn't last long at all. I just kind of sigh, fix my foundation a bit, and get right back to work. 

I definitely don't let it ruin my day or anything like that. I'm usually very positive! I hope that's what you were asking? I just really want to be clear that I'm not falling apart over this or anything.
Have there been times when you avoided social situations, events, or even certain people because you were particularly worried about how your face looked?

Oh, avoid things? No, no, I wouldn't say I avoid people or events. I'm very reliable! I still get all my work done at the firm, and I make sure I'm there when people need me. I don't want you to think I'm just hiding away in my house or anything. 

I mean, I guess... well, there have been a few mornings where I spent a little extra time getting ready, just trying to make sure my makeup was sitting right, and maybe I had to rush into the courthouse a bit fast. And... I suppose I've missed the very beginning of my yoga class a couple of times because of that, too. But I always show up! 

And, um, like I mentioned before about the pictures... I have skipped being in a few casual group photos at my book club, or at some community events. Just because... well, I didn't want to spend the whole time worrying about how my face was going to look in them. It's easier just to step out of the frame, you know? But I'm still at the events, participating and having a good time. I hope that makes sense? I just really want to assure you that I'm keeping up with my life just fine.

Can you tell me if there have been days when you felt so concerned about how your face looks that it was hard to focus on anything else, or that it really interfered with your ability to do your job or enjoy your day?

Oh, goodness, no. I really wouldn't say that at all. I mean... I'm a paralegal, so my job requires a lot of attention to detail, and I would never let something like this get in the way of my work. The attorneys rely on me too much, you know? 

So, no, it definitely doesn't make it hard to focus or interfere with my job. I promise I'm very dedicated to the firm. And as for enjoying my day... well, I still have a lovely time! Like I said, I still go to my yoga classes and my book club. I might have a... a brief moment where I wish my skin looked a bit firmer or more even, but I just push it right out of my mind and get back to what I'm doing. 

I really wouldn't let it consume my thoughts or ruin my day. I'm a very grounded person. I hope that reassures you? I just really don't want you to think I'm sitting at my desk obsessing over my face when I should be working. Does that answer your question okay?
Have you been feeling down, sad, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy, even outside of concerns about your appearance?

Oh, sad? No, no, I wouldn't say that. I really don't feel down or depressed at all. I'm a very upbeat person, honestly! 

I still love doing all the things I usually do. My book club is wonderful, and yoga always makes me feel so refreshed. I definitely haven't lost interest in any of that. I mean, life is busy, of course, and sometimes I'm just a little tired after a long week at the firm, but that's just normal, right? 

I really try to look on the bright side of things. I wouldn't want you to think I'm sitting around feeling sorry for myself or anything like that. I'm very happy with my life, I promise. Is that... is that the kind of thing you were asking about? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Can you tell me if you ever feel anxious or self-conscious in social situations because of how your face looks, even when you're not actively looking at yourself?

Oh, anxious? Um... well, I wouldn't use the word anxious. That sounds so... intense, you know? I really don't feel like I'm sitting there panicking or anything. 

I mean, maybe... occasionally, if I'm talking to someone new at a community event, I might just have a passing thought about whether they're noticing my skin or the little lines around my eyes. But it's just a tiny, fleeting thing! I just smile and keep the conversation going, and it's perfectly fine. I don't let it ruin the interaction at all. 

I really try to focus on being polite and making the other person feel comfortable. I'm very good at keeping things professional and pleasant. I definitely wouldn't say I'm noticeably self-conscious or awkward. I hope that makes sense? I just want to be clear that I handle social situations very well. Does that answer what you were looking for?

Can you tell me if there have been times when your concern about your facial appearance made you feel so upset that you had trouble functioning normally, like difficulty concentrating at work or withdrawing from people completely?

Oh, goodness, no! "Trouble functioning normally" sounds so... severe. I promise I haven't withdrawn from people completely or anything like that. I still get all my work done, and the attorneys are very happy with me. I would never let things fall apart. 

I mean... I suppose, if I'm being completely honest... sometimes I do spend a little extra time getting ready in the mornings. Just to make sure everything looks as neat and presentable as possible, you know? And, well, I guess that extra time has made me have to rush into the courthouse a few mornings. And... I might have missed the first few minutes of my yoga class more than once because I was running a bit behind. But I always get there! 

And I guess... well, at book club and those community events I mentioned, I have skipped being in a few of the casual photos lately. Just because I didn't want to worry about how my face would look in them. It’s just easier to offer to be the one taking the picture, right? 

But I’m definitely not withdrawing completely or letting it ruin my work! I still show up for everything and participate. I hope that’s okay? I just really want you to know I'm still handling my responsibilities well and functioning just fine. Did I explain that alright?

Can you tell me if your concerns about your facial appearance have ever caused you to spend so much time on checking or fixing your appearance that it significantly interfered with your daily routine or responsibilities?

Oh, "significantly interfered" is a strong way to put it. I wouldn't say it interferes, really. I always get everything done! 

I mean, I did mention that I take a little extra time in the mornings, right? Most days, before I leave for the courthouse, I just... you know, I check my face from a few different angles in the mirror. Just to be sure. And I might put on a little extra makeup, just to smooth things out so I look professional. It’s important to look put-together at a law firm! 

And, well, I guess sometimes when I'm at work, I might catch myself looking at the other women there, just... comparing a little bit. Seeing how their skin looks compared to mine. But it's nothing major, I promise! It doesn't stop me from doing my job. 

And like I said before, I do sometimes avoid being in those casual pictures at events if I'm not feeling great about how I look that day. But I'm still there, participating and helping out! I really don't let it take over my whole routine. Is that... does that make sense? I hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is, because I really do keep up with all my responsibilities!

Can you recall a time when your concern about your facial appearance caused you noticeable emotional distress or made it hard for you to function in any important area of life, like work, socializing, or personal relationships?

Oh, um... no, I really can't think of anything like that. "Noticeable emotional distress" sounds just so... so heavy, you know? Like crying or not being able to get out of bed, and I promise I've never had anything like that happen. 

My relationships are wonderful. The ladies at book club are lovely, and the attorneys I work for are always telling me how reliable I am. I would never let a silly worry about my face get in the way of my job or my friendships. I mean, sure, I might get a tiny bit frustrated if my makeup isn't sitting right in the morning, but it's just a normal, everyday frustration. It definitely doesn't make it hard to function! 

I'm always very careful to make sure I'm doing my part and being a good friend and a good employee. I really pride myself on being dependable, no matter what. Does that make sense? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of answers... I really just want to be helpful!
Have you ever had to change your plans, cancel something important, or significantly alter how you live your life because of how much you worry about your facial appearance?

Oh, absolutely not! Change my plans or cancel something important? No, I would never do that. That sounds so... irresponsible, and I really try my best to always be reliable. 

I mean, if I say I'm going to be somewhere, I'm going to be there. Like I mentioned, I might be a tiny bit late to yoga sometimes because I'm just making sure I look presentable, but I never cancel! And I've never missed a day of work because of this, ever. The attorneys count on me, and I would hate to let them down over something so... trivial as worrying about my face. 

I really haven't altered how I live my life at all. I still do everything I've always done. I just... maybe I just do it with a little more makeup on, or while standing behind the camera instead of in front of it. But I'm still living my life exactly the same way! 

I really try to be a good, dependable person, and I wouldn't let this get in the way of that. I hope that's what you're looking for? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.

Can you tell me if there have been days when your concern about how your face looks was so intense that it made it hard for you to enjoy your day, focus on your work, or engage in social situations—even briefly?

Oh... well... "intense" is a bit much, I think. I really do always get my work done! I make sure of that. But... I suppose, if I'm being completely honest... maybe just briefly? 

Like, because of the extra time I spend getting ready, there have been a few mornings where I had to rush into the courthouse. Just a little rushed, I still got right to my desk! And, um, I have missed the very start of my yoga class more than once. Just the warm-up part at the beginning, though.

Does that make sense? I hope I'm not repeating myself too much, I just want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you need!

Is... is that what you were asking? I'm so sorry if I'm making you repeat yourself. I really am trying to give you the best answers I can!

Oh, um... well, I wouldn't say a *lot* of time. I know some people can just obsess over mirrors all day, and I'm definitely not like that! I'm way too busy at the firm for that kind of thing.

Oh... "real emotional pain"? Oh my goodness, no, I wouldn't say that at all. That sounds so... heavy! I really hope I haven't been making it sound like I'm sitting around crying or anything like that. I'm actually a very positive person! 

I mean, sure, I get a little frustrated sometimes, like I mentioned with the mornings, but... truly upset? No, never. I always try to just count my blessings and get on with my day. I know how lucky I am to have a good job and great friends, so I'd never let myself get genuinely pained over how I look. It's really just a minor annoyance, I promise. 

Is it okay that I don't have that? I just want to make sure I'm giving you an accurate picture and not making things sound worse than they actually are!
Can you tell me if your concern about your facial appearance has ever caused problems in your relationships, job performance, or participation in important life activities, even briefly?

Oh, um... well, no, I wouldn't call them *problems*, exactly. I mean, I still get all my work done at the firm, and the attorneys are very happy with me! I would never let anything really impact my job. 

I guess... well, like I said, the extra time I spend getting ready in the mornings has made me a little rushed getting to the courthouse a few times. But it's nothing major! I'm still very active and involved in everything. I hope that doesn't sound like it's causing real problems? I'm just trying to be completely honest with you!
